note: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH (spec §13). Every gate and the site itself read this file.
Pixel positions are NOT stored — they are derived from `constants` by milestoneY() in src/lib/timeline.ts,
so a date cannot be verified in one place and shipped from another.
Genus names are marked with *asterisks* and rendered as <em>; the plain-text form is what a screen reader gets.
Sections still to be filled by their own build steps: field keyframes (§6), solved scrims (solve-scrim.ts),

arrivals.name: The Solar System forms
arrivals.line: Dust and ice collapse around a new star. Nothing older has ever been dated.
arrivals.analogy: a fist-sized slice of stony meteorite, cut and polished flat: a dark grey matrix studded with a scatter of pale chalky-white, irregular rounded blobs a centimetre or two across
arrivals.negative: not a planet, not a swirling disc of dust and gas, not a starfield — one physical rock, cut open and held still, the oldest dated solid material in the solar system rather than an artist's impression of its birth. The matrix stays a mid-to-dark grey, never black or near-black, or the luminance key punches holes through it; the pale inclusions are chalky white-grey, dull, not glowing and not metallic.
arrivals.reference: Allende meteorite CAI specimen photographs — AMNH 4880 (amnh.org); Connelly et al. 2012, *Science*

arrivals.name: Earth reaches full size
arrivals.line: Accretion finishes. The whole surface is molten rock.
arrivals.analogy: a ball of liquid rock, glowing orange-red, brighter yellow-white cracks, a few darker cooling crusts floating on it
arrivals.negative: not a rocky planet with lava rivers

arrivals.name: The Moon is torn out
arrivals.line: A Mars-sized body strikes, at least 4.51 billion years ago. The debris becomes a Moon that hangs enormous and close.
arrivals.analogy: a small sphere of molten rock hanging alone against black, dull orange-red overall with brighter cracks of yellow-white light breaking through its surface
arrivals.negative: not the grey, cratered Moon of today — freshly torn from Earth it is still glowing rock, the same register as the Earth-full-size portrait rather than a rocky moon. Nothing on it may be black or near-black; darker patches read as dimmer glow, never as dark holes or shadow.
arrivals.reference: giant-impact hypothesis reconstructions (NASA/SwRI simulation renders); styled to match the molten-Hadean Earth portrait already baked, §11

arrivals.line: The Moon is two and a half times wider than it is today

arrivals.name: Liquid water
arrivals.line: A single zircon crystal records water at the surface.
arrivals.analogy: one tiny gem-like crystal shown much larger than life, reddish-brown and translucent, a slender six-sided prism with pointed pyramidal ends, alone against black
arrivals.negative: not a boulder, not a cluster, not a vein in rock — a single isolated crystal, magnified the way a specimen diagram magnifies something smaller than a grain of rice. Reddish-brown to amber and translucent, never black or near-black, and never cut with flat gemstone facets — natural crystal faces only.
arrivals.reference: Jack Hills zircon grain photomicrographs — Cavosie et al. 2018 review figures; Wilde et al. 2001, *Nature*

arrivals.name: Steam and acid rain
arrivals.line: The air is CO₂. The rain is acid. There is nothing yet you would call land.
arrivals.analogy: a single pitted, etched volcanic rock in mid-toned warm grey and rust, its pits shown as shallow dents a shade or two darker than the surface, with pale streaks of rain running down its face
arrivals.negative: not a landscape or a storm scene — one rock specimen and nothing else in its quarter of the picture, no loose fragments or stray marks floating near it. Nothing anywhere on the rock may be black or near-black: the pits are mid-grey dents, not dark holes, and the rock overall is a light-to-mid value. The rain is drawn as pale streaks ON the rock's face, running down it. Two rounds (2026-07-31): the first was near-black and the key punched every pit out of the artwork; the second keyed correctly but lost the rain and left a stray orange fragment floating above the rock.

arrivals.name: The oldest surviving crust
arrivals.line: Nuvvuagittuq, Quebec — a scrap of the first ocean floor.
arrivals.analogy: a hand-sized slab of grey-beige banded rock, its bands running in soft parallel waves, with a scatter of small dark purple-red garnet flecks caught in the pale bands
arrivals.negative: not dark green like an ordinary amphibolite — this rock's whole identity is that it is paler than the rock it resembles ('faux'-amphibolite). The base colour is light grey-beige, never black or near-black, and the banding is soft and wavy, not tightly folded like the Rodinia gneiss elsewhere on this page.
arrivals.reference: Nuvvuagittuq faux-amphibolite specimen photographs — sciencemall-usa.com; Flickr (jsjgeology); O'Neil et al. 2025, *Science*

arrivals.name: The oldest rock we still have
arrivals.line: Acasta gneiss, north-west Canada. The Hadean ends here because this is where the record starts.
arrivals.analogy: a hand-sized slab of streaky rock, straight alternating bands of pale pinkish-grey and darker brownish-grey, with a few small red garnet flecks
arrivals.negative: not tightly folded like the later Rodinia gneiss elsewhere on this page — these bands run straighter and more evenly striped. The darker bands stay a mid brownish-grey, never black or near-black.
arrivals.reference: Acasta Gneiss specimen photographs — Prince of Wales Northern Heritage Centre; C&EN 2023 (cen.acs.org)

arrivals.name: The oldest sedimentary rocks
arrivals.line: Isua, Greenland — mud, laid down under water, by a real ocean.
arrivals.analogy: a hand-sized slab of fine-grained rock split along its bedding, showing dozens of thin, slightly wavy parallel layers stacked like the pages of a closed book, pale grey-green throughout
arrivals.negative: not the bold red-and-black striping of a banded iron formation — that is a different, later rock on this page. These layers are finer, closer together and all in a narrow grey-green range: the record of ordinary mud settling in water, not iron precipitating out of it. Nothing in the layers may be black or near-black.
arrivals.reference: Isua supracrustal belt metasediment specimen photographs — FossilEra; Nutman et al. 1997, *Precambrian Res.*

arrivals.name: The first trace of life
arrivals.line: Isotopically light carbon in Isua sediment. Not a fossil — a chemical shadow, and the oldest one anyone accepts.
arrivals.analogy: the same pale grey-green layered rock as the Isua sediment beside it on this page — a cool sage grey-green overall, with no warm buff or brown in it — scattered with dull mid-grey graphite flecks — short angular slivers and smears lying along the layering, like pencil lead rubbed into stone, never round bubbles or holes
arrivals.negative: not a fossil and not any visible shape of a living thing — the evidence is chemical, a carbon isotope ratio, not a body, so nothing organism-shaped may appear anywhere on the rock. The graphite specks are dull dark grey, never black or near-black, or the luminance key punches them out of the artwork. First round (2026-08-01): the rock itself matched, but it shared a sheet with Tiktaalik in the adjacent quadrant, whose snout sat hard against the sheet's vertical midline and bled a sliver of orange across it — inflating this quadrant's trimmed bounding box to 779×623 against its sibling rock's 600×501. Not a fault of this subject's own prompt; redo needs its neighbour drawn with real clearance from the boundary, not a change to this description.
arrivals.reference: Isua metasediment graphite-inclusion specimen photographs (same locality as the oldest sedimentary rocks); Rosing 1999, *Science*; Ohtomo et al. 2014

arrivals.name: Microbial mats
arrivals.line: Life is a film on the seabed, and stays that way for three billion years.
arrivals.analogy: a broad, low, wrinkled sheet lying flat on sediment, like the crumpled skin on cooled paint — a deep olive-green overall, its margins flushed dull pink-purple where the sulfur-bacteria layer beneath shows through, puckered into ridges and shallow domes a few centimetres across
arrivals.negative: not coral, not seaweed, not any branching or upright growth: a microbial mat is a flat film ON the sediment, with no stems, fronds or plant-like structure. Not a stromatolite either — no built-up column and no internal layering, those arrive later on this page. Keep it light-to-mid in value; the shadows between wrinkles are shallow dents, never near-black.
arrivals.reference: modern Shark Bay and Sippewissett microbial mat photographs; Noffke et al. 2013, *Astrobiology*

arrivals.name: Stromatolites
arrivals.line: Mats build the first structures life leaves behind. Whether these particular ones did is still argued.
arrivals.analogy: a rounded, layered mound of banded rock, like a stack of thin stone plates or a cross-section of a cabbage
arrivals.negative: not a mushroom, not a shell, not a visible living creature — a banded rock structure
arrivals.source: Dresser Fm. 3.48 Ga; Baumgartner et al. 2024

arrivals.name: Microbes that eat sulfur
arrivals.line: No oxygen, no sunlight needed — chemistry alone.
arrivals.analogy: a cluster of tiny rod- and sphere-shaped cells at high magnification, translucent pale yellow-green, each scattered with vivid lemon-yellow sulfur granules inside it like mustard seeds suspended in glass — the whole cluster reads as a bright clean lemon-yellow
arrivals.negative: not a plant, not an animal, not anything with a body plan — these are single cells. Not chlorophyll-green leafy algae: the colour comes from sulfur, so it reads pale yellow and warm. No cell may be near-black, and the granules must stay bright.
arrivals.reference: Wacey et al. 2011, *Nature Geoscience* — Strelley Pool microfossils; modern sulfur-oxidising bacteria light micrographs

arrivals.name: A fifty-kilometre asteroid
arrivals.line: The S2 impact — 50 to 200 times the mass of the one that killed the dinosaurs. It boils the top of the ocean, and life gets better.
arrivals.analogy: one irregular rock tumbling alone, clearly longer than it is wide like a potato or a peanut rather than a ball, pitted all over with shallow overlapping craters like Phobos, a cool neutral blue-grey throughout with no warm brown or tan in it
arrivals.negative: not a fireball, not a streaking meteor with a flame trail, and not an impact scene with Earth in frame — this is the body itself, a single cratered rock. Not a warm sandstone-tan asteroid, which is the default: a stony body photographs a cool neutral grey, like Phobos and Bennu. Craters are shallow dents a shade or two darker, never black holes, or the luminance key punches them out of the artwork.
arrivals.reference: Phobos and Bennu spacecraft imagery; Drabon et al. 2024, *PNAS* — S2 impactor, 37–58 km

arrivals.name: The first continents
arrivals.line: Cratons stabilise. There is now permanent dry land.
arrivals.analogy: a hand-sized block of coarse granite, dominantly a warm salmon-pink from its large blocky feldspar crystals — angular interlocking grains of clearly different sizes, jammed against one another rather than evenly-spaced round dots — set with glassy grey quartz and small pale mica flecks; the light, buoyant rock continents are made of
arrivals.negative: not the fine dark banding of a gneiss: the oldest rock elsewhere on this page is a gneiss and these two must not read as the same specimen. Granite is coarse and speckled, never layered. Not a landscape, not an island, not a map — one hand specimen. Mica flecks are mid-grey, never black.
arrivals.reference: coarse-grained granite hand-specimen photographs; Hawkesworth et al. 2020

arrivals.name: Photosynthesis
arrivals.line: Cyanobacteria split water and let the oxygen go. It will take 600 million years to matter.
arrivals.source: Sánchez-Baracaldo et al. 2021, *Proc. R. Soc. B*
arrivals.analogy: a single gently curved filament of cells strung end to end like a string of beads inside a clear sheath, each cell a rounded cylinder, the whole filament a strong blue-green teal
arrivals.negative: not a plant, not a leaf, not seaweed — a cyanobacterium is one filament of cells. Not grass-green: the colour is a distinctive blue-green. The sheath is translucent, not a dark outline, and no cell may be near-black.
arrivals.reference: modern *Oscillatoria* and *Nostoc* light micrographs; Sánchez-Baracaldo et al. 2021, *Proc. R. Soc. B*

arrivals.name: The first ice age
arrivals.line: The Pongola glaciation. Ice at mid-latitudes, on a planet with no oxygen.
arrivals.source: Young et al. 1998; Ojakangas et al. 2014
arrivals.analogy: a broken block of diamictite the colour of wet slate — sharp-cornered pebbles of many different sizes jammed at all angles into a fine stony matrix, like fruitcake turned to stone — with one flat face bearing straight parallel scratches where ice dragged it across bedrock; the whole rock a cold blue-grey with no warm brown in it
arrivals.negative: not a snowy landscape, not a glacier and not an iceberg: the evidence for the first ice age is a rock. Not a ball, not a sphere and not a smooth beach cobble — it is an angular broken lump with flat fractured faces and sharp corners, and the embedded clasts are angular and unsorted, never round spots. It must not read as a planet or a moon seen from space; three planet portraits elsewhere on this page own that shape. The scratches are shallow grooves, never black lines.
arrivals.reference: glacial diamictite and striated pavement specimen photographs; Young et al. 1998; Ojakangas et al. 2014

arrivals.name: Cyanobacteria, everywhere
arrivals.line: Still no free oxygen in the air — the rock is drinking all of it.
arrivals.analogy: a loose drifting raft of many filaments lying across one another in a flat open layer, each filament plainly made of rounded cells stacked end to end like a string of beads with the separate cells clearly visible, the whole raft a deep blue-green teal — the same colour and the same beaded strands as the single filament earlier on this page
arrivals.negative: the same organism as the photosynthesis subject earlier on this page, drawn as a crowd rather than one strand, and it must read as the same material. Not a ball of yarn, wool, string or knitted thread, which is the default for a tangle: the filaments are never smooth cords, every one is visibly a row of separate round cells. Not a tight sphere or a bundle — the raft is flat and loosely spread, with filaments crossing over each other and free ends drifting out. Not a plant, not seaweed, not leafy, not branching. No dark outlines and nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: as photosynthesis — modern *Oscillatoria* and *Nostoc* light micrographs

arrivals.name: Whiffs of oxygen
arrivals.line: Oxygen appears in patches, hundreds of millions of years before the air changes.
arrivals.analogy: a cluster of small bubbles rising off a mat of green scum, like carbonation
arrivals.negative: not fire or an explosion — gas bubbles, not flame

arrivals.line: The sky flickers orange and back, three to five times
arrivals.source: Zerkle et al. 2012; Izon et al. 2015, 2017

arrivals.name: Banded iron
arrivals.line: Oxygen meets dissolved iron and it rusts out of the sea, in bands, for a billion years.
arrivals.analogy: a cut block of banded iron formation standing on end, crossed by dozens of narrow wavy parallel bands — deep brick-red and maroon jasper alternating with silver-grey iron layers, the bands gently folded, varying in thickness, some pinching out and some swelling; the dominant colour is a deep brick-red
arrivals.negative: not a cliff, canyon or landscape, and not an abstract stripe pattern: one hand-sized specimen with rough broken edges. Not the fine even grey-green layering of the Isua sediment elsewhere on this page — these bands are bold, red and high-contrast. The silver-grey bands are a mid-tone metallic grey, never black.
arrivals.reference: banded iron formation hand-specimen photographs (Hamersley, Marquette); Bekker et al. 2010, *Econ. Geol.*

arrivals.name: Banded iron, still
arrivals.line: Still rusting out of the sea. It has been a hundred million years.
arrivals.analogy: the same banded iron formation as earlier on this page, drawn as a broader, thicker slab — many more red-and-silver bands stacked across it, the layering denser and the folding tighter; the dominant colour is again a deep brick-red
arrivals.negative: the same rock as the 2,600 Ma banded iron and it must read as the same material: deep brick-red jasper alternating with metallic silver-grey. Not a bright scarlet or fire-red — the red is dark and earthy. The silver bands are a neutral metallic grey, never blue or blue-grey and never black. Not a landscape and not a stripe pattern.
arrivals.reference: as banded-iron — Bekker et al. 2010, *Econ. Geol.*

arrivals.name: The Great Oxidation begins
arrivals.line: Free oxygen floods the air and poisons most of the life that made it.
arrivals.analogy: smooth and featureless like Titan, thick orange-tan haze, faint soft banding, no continents or oceans visible
arrivals.negative: not Jupiter — no bold stripes, no storms

arrivals.name: The Huronian glaciation
arrivals.line: Oxygen destroys the methane greenhouse and the planet freezes, three times over.
arrivals.analogy: a single dark slate-grey boulder half-buried in fine layered pale grey-green mud, punched down into it so the layers directly beneath are pushed into a deep U-shaped sag under its weight while the layers above drape up and over it — a dropstone, the signature of ice rafting; the dominant colour is a cool grey-green, with no warm buff or orange anywhere in it
arrivals.negative: not a snowy scene, not a glacier and not an iceberg: the evidence is a rock. The boulder is embedded in the mud, never resting on top of a flat slab like an ornament on a plinth, and the layers beneath it must visibly bend down into a bowl around it — that deformation is the whole point of the specimen and the only thing that proves the stone fell. Gently wavy ripples are not enough. Not the striated boulder used for the first ice age earlier on this page — this one sits in sediment. Nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: Gowganda Formation dropstone photographs; Young 2013

arrivals.line: The sky is blue

arrivals.name: The Great Oxidation ends
arrivals.line: Oxygen is permanent. The haze never comes back.
arrivals.analogy: a rust-red rock slab seen close, with a crack of open blue sky at the top
arrivals.negative: not a full landscape — one slab, the sky a sliver behind it

arrivals.name: Francevillian structures?
arrivals.line: Centimetre-scale shapes in Gabon. Possibly the oldest multicellular life; possibly not life at all.
arrivals.analogy: several flat, lobed, coin-sized discs on a slab of cool slate-grey mudstone with a faint violet cast, each disc a pale pyritic cream with a wrinkled, crumpled raised rim and a smoother middle, its outline irregular and lobed like a blob of dried wax pressed into the rock; the dominant colour is a cool violet-grey, never buff or brown
arrivals.negative: not a fossil animal, not a shell, and nothing with recognisable body parts — whether these are life at all is disputed, so they must read as ambiguous shapes in rock rather than as a creature. Not regular circles like coins: the outlines are irregular and lobed. Nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: El Albani et al. 2010, *Nature*; El Albani et al. 2014, *PLoS ONE* — Francevillian B specimens

arrivals.line: Oxygen falls back

arrivals.name: *Grypania*?
arrivals.line: A coiled ribbon in Michigan iron. Big enough to see, but nothing of its cells survives.
arrivals.analogy: a single flat ribbon lying on an unbanded slab of dark rust-red iron-rich rock as one large open ring, like a rubber band or a loop of tape dropped flat on a table — a wide empty circle of bare rock in the middle of the loop, one end of the ribbon visibly stopping short and lapping past the other so it reads as a length of ribbon rather than a closed circle, the loop slightly uneven the way a dropped band lies rather than a perfect machined circle, the ribbon exactly the same width from one end to the other — a flat matte pewter-grey film pressed into the face of the rock and flush with it, stained into the stone rather than sitting on it
arrivals.negative: not a shell and not an ammonite: no chambers, no ribs, no ridges. It is not a spiral at all and the word does not apply: it does not wind inward, it has no centre and it makes no second or third turn. It is ONE ring with a large hole of bare rock in the middle. Two rounds (2026-08-01) both drew a tight spiral wound inward like a snail, a nautilus or a carved petroglyph — the second did so even while being told not to, so the redo dropped the words spiral, coil and curl entirely and asked for a ring, which worked. Round three then over-corrected into a perfectly circular raised metal washer or gasket lying on top of a pebble: it is not a manufactured object, not polished, not metallic, not three-dimensional and not separable from the rock — it is a flat carbonaceous stain in the rock face, level with the surface, and its two ends must be findable. The ribbon never tapers or narrows; it is the same width the whole way. It is a smooth featureless ribbon, and nothing of its internal structure survives. Not a worm with a head or segments. Not the striped red-and-silver block of banded iron elsewhere on this page — this slab is a plain unbanded rust-red with no layering. The carbon film reads mid-grey against the red rock, never near-black, or the luminance key punches it out.
arrivals.reference: Han & Runnegar 1992, *Science* — *Grypania spiralis*, Negaunee Iron Formation

arrivals.line: Banded iron stops
arrivals.source: Bekker et al. 2010 — end of major BIF

arrivals.name: The first complex cells
arrivals.line: *Qingshania* — cells with a nucleus, stuck together on purpose.
arrivals.analogy: a short straight filament of seven or eight large box-shaped cells joined end to end like the carriages of a train, each cell a translucent fresh grass-green and far chunkier than a bacterium, holding one softly-defined rounded body inside it
arrivals.negative: not a plant, not a leaf and not seaweed. Not the blue-green of the cyanobacteria earlier on this page — this is a clear grass-green. Not a thin bacterial thread — the whole point is that these cells are large and compartmented, each carrying a nucleus, so they must look chunky and blocky rather than hair-like. The nucleus is a soft mid-toned disc, never a black dot.
arrivals.reference: Miao et al. 2024, *Sci. Adv.* — *Qingshania magnifica*

arrivals.name: Sex
arrivals.line: *Bangiomorpha*, a red alga. The oldest known sexual reproduction.
arrivals.analogy: a short upright tuft of red alga in a deep saturated wine-red, almost purple: a single unbranched filament of stacked disc-shaped cells, like a narrow pile of coins, anchored at its base by a small holdfast
arrivals.negative: not a leafy frond, not kelp and not a branching plant — *Bangiomorpha* is one narrow filament of stacked cells on a holdfast. Not green: it is a red alga, and its colour is a deep saturated wine-red verging on purple, not a pale or washed pink. No dark outline and nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: Gibson et al. 2018, *Geology*; modern *Bangia* micrographs — *Bangiomorpha pubescens*

arrivals.name: Rodinia
arrivals.line: Every continent, gathered into one mass.
arrivals.analogy: a specimen of folded gneiss — a banded rock whose pink, grey and pale mineral stripes are bent into tight parallel folds, as if the layers had been squeezed from both sides
arrivals.negative: not a map, not a landmass, not a continent and not a globe — one rock specimen seen close. The bands are smooth continuous folded stripes, not cracks and not loose brushstrokes. Nothing anywhere on it may be black or near-black. Two rounds (2026-07-31) drew the modern African continent, with Madagascar, when this milestone was prompted as a landmass silhouette — a negative naming Africa did not stop it. The subject is therefore the rock that continental collision makes (the Grenville orogeny, ~1.1–0.9 Ga, is Rodinia's assembly) rather than the shape of the supercontinent.

arrivals.name: The first sponges?
arrivals.line: Sponge-like structures in Canadian reef rock, 300 million years before any agreed animal.
arrivals.analogy: a lump of warm honey-cream reef limestone sliced open on one flat cut face, and that whole cut face filled edge to edge with a dense fine mesh of hundreds of thin rust-orange worm-like tubes, tangled and winding at every angle and far too many to count — the vermicular texture inside a bath sponge, or a plate of tangled thread
arrivals.negative: not a modern vase- or barrel-shaped sponge sitting on a reef: what survives is a microscopic meshwork inside rock, and the identification is disputed, so this is a rock specimen with a tube network in it rather than an animal. Not one bold branching tree or a few thick piped lines drawn on the outside of a pebble, which is the default: the tubes are fine, numerous and crowded, and they are the exposed interior of the rock rather than a pattern on its skin. The tubes are mid-toned, never near-black holes.
arrivals.reference: Turner 2021, *Nature* — Little Dal reef vermiform microstructure

arrivals.line: The Boring Billion ends

arrivals.name: Snowball Earth
arrivals.line: Ice reaches the tropics. The Sturtian lasts 56 million years.
arrivals.analogy: ice pole to pole, pale blue-grey fracture lines like cracked porcelain, a few small bare rock patches near the middle
arrivals.negative: not a modern Earth with white poles and blue oceans

arrivals.name: The ice retreats
arrivals.line: Cap carbonate, laid down in a few thousand years on top of the ice.
arrivals.analogy: a slab of cool pale grey-cream limestone with a faint blue cast, in fine even layers, its top surface crossed by low rounded parallel ripples like ripples in wet sand, never a zigzag or chevron pattern, sitting sharply on a rougher darker rock beneath — the boundary between the two flat and abrupt; the dominant colour is a cool pale grey-cream, never a warm buff or honey
arrivals.negative: not an iceberg, not a glacier and not melting ice: the evidence is the rock that formed on top of what the ice left. Not the red-and-silver banding of banded iron — cap carbonate is pale, creamy and finely layered. The rock beneath stays mid-toned, never black.
arrivals.reference: Marinoan and Sturtian cap carbonate outcrop and hand-specimen photographs; Rooney et al. 2015, *Geology*

arrivals.name: The ice breaks for good
arrivals.line: A second freeze, the Marinoan — perhaps only four million years — and then it is over. The Ediacaran begins.
arrivals.source: ICS base Ediacaran 635.0 Ma; Wang et al. 2025, *PNAS*
arrivals.analogy: a broken block of dark slate blue-grey glacial diamictite whose top half gives way to smooth even meltwater-laid bedding in pale ice-blue — jumbled sharp-cornered pebbles of all sizes jammed in at every angle below, quiet flat layers above, with a clean line between them
arrivals.negative: not a landscape, not an ice sheet and not a thaw scene: one rock specimen recording the transition. It must read as the same family of glacial rock as the earlier ice subjects on this page. Nothing near-black between the clasts.
arrivals.reference: Marinoan diamictite–cap carbonate contact specimens; ICS base Ediacaran 635.0 Ma; Wang et al. 2025, *PNAS*

arrivals.name: *Charnia*
arrivals.line: The first big bodies — soft, strange, rooted to the seabed.
arrivals.analogy: a frond like a fern or chestnut leaf, branching ridges repeating as smaller copies of themselves down its length, rooted to the seabed by a small disc
arrivals.negative: not a plant or seaweed — no leaves branching off a stem, one long frond of self-similar ridges

arrivals.name: The Cambrian begins
arrivals.line: Shells, eyes, guts, predators, and the first things burrowing through mud on purpose.
arrivals.analogy: a trilobite seen from directly above: a flat oval shield divided lengthwise into three lobes, a broad crescent head with a raised ridge running down its middle and one crescent eye on the cheek either side of that ridge, a jointed thorax of repeated segments, and a small tail plate, the whole shield a deep violet-blue with pale cream margins along its rim
arrivals.negative: not a woodlouse, not a horseshoe crab and not a beetle — the three lengthwise lobes and the crescent head shield are the defining shapes and must be unmistakable. No insect antennae. The dominant colour is a deep violet-blue with pale cream margins — never brown, orange or rust, which is the default, and never near-black.
arrivals.reference: *Olenellus* and *Paradoxides* specimen photographs; ICS 2023 — 538.8 ± 0.6 Ma

arrivals.name: The Burgess Shale
arrivals.line: *Anomalocaris* — a metre of segmented predator, with the first real eyes.
arrivals.analogy: a flattened, segmented swimmer with rows of side fins like a shrimp, two large stalked eyes, two long spiny grasping arms held out in front like a pair of curved combs, and underneath the head a small circular ring of overlapping plates, like a camera aperture, as its mouth
arrivals.negative: no pincers, no crab or lobster claws, no snapping jaws of any kind — the front arms are segmented and spiny like a centipede's legs held forward, not a claw that closes shut; the mouth is a round plated ring facing DOWN, not a mouth on the front of the face. First round (2026-07-31) drew a lobster with pincer claws and a jawed mouth — exactly what this negative forbids. Redo needed with this stronger wording.

arrivals.name: Plants reach land
arrivals.line: Spores, nothing you could call a plant yet. Land has been bare for four billion years.
arrivals.analogy: a flat microscope slide view of a cryptospore tetrad in transmitted light: four thin-walled circles overlapping in a clover, drawn flat with no volume and no roundness at all, their walls a fine darker amber line that thickens where the four press together, their interiors a pale washed translucent amber you can see straight through, the whole group finely stippled like frosted glass
arrivals.negative: not a plant, not a leaf, not a stem and not moss: at this date there is nothing anyone would call a plant, only spores. Not oranges, tangerines, citrus or fruit of any kind, which is the default for a cluster of round objects — a low proof of this subject (2026-08-01) came back as three oranges, so the surface is glassy and translucent like frosted glass, never opaque dimpled peel. Exactly four, never three, and they are bonded into one body rather than resting against each other. Not a single sphere — the diagnostic is the bonded group of four. Three rounds (2026-08-01) all drew solid opaque orange balls, because spherical shading is what makes a cluster of round objects read as fruit: so there is NO volume shading, NO gloss, NO specular highlight and NO cast shading of any kind here. This is a flat two-dimensional graphic of a translucent thing seen with light coming through it from behind, closer to a stained-glass roundel than to a painted sphere. Keep it warm translucent amber, never near-black.
arrivals.reference: Rubinstein et al. 2010, *New Phytol.* — Ordovician cryptospore tetrads

arrivals.name: The Late Ordovician extinction
arrivals.line: Ice, then anoxia. About 85% of species go.
arrivals.analogy: several graptolite fossils fanning out from one point on a neutral pale grey shale slab with no warm or brown cast — each a narrow straight strip edged with fine regular teeth, like the blade of a hacksaw flattened into the rock, the fossil film a silvery mid-grey against the paler slab
arrivals.negative: not a plant, not a fern frond and not a feather: graptolites are straight or gently curved toothed strips preserved as a flattened film. The film must read as a mid-tone silvery grey against a lighter slab, never black, or the luminance key punches it out of the artwork.
arrivals.reference: *Dicellograptus* and *Climacograptus* specimen photographs; Harper et al. 2014

arrivals.name: *Cooksonia*
arrivals.line: The first plants with stems. A few centimetres tall, and the tallest thing alive.
arrivals.analogy: a few centimetres of forking, leafless green stems, splitting into two even branches again and again, with small rounded capsules at the branch tips
arrivals.negative: not a plant with leaves or roots — bare forking stems only, nothing frond-like or leafy

arrivals.name: *Tiktaalik*
arrivals.line: A fish with a neck, and wrists.
arrivals.analogy: a coelacanth seen from directly overhead, lying flat on a stream bed and looked straight down upon from above: the same heavy scales, the same broad three-lobed tail, the same deep steel-blue mottled with pale blue-white flecks, and a pair of thick fleshy-based front fins spread out to either side, each ending in a fan of stiff fin-rays — and at the front, instead of an ordinary fish head, a broad flat spade much wider than the body, with both eyes sitting up on the flat top surface of it near the middle, looking straight up out of the picture at the viewer
arrivals.negative: not standing, not walking, not upright on four legs, and not a salamander, newt, lizard, amphibian or frog. The whole animal lies flat and horizontal in the water, exactly like the coelacanth it is drawn from — the head is the one place it departs from an ordinary coelacanth, wider and flatter, with the eyes on the very top looking up rather than out to the sides. Every fin ends in a smooth unbroken fan of fin-rays — no toes, no fingers, no claws, nothing hand-shaped or foot-shaped anywhere on the animal. Four rounds (2026-07-31) each held one half of the animal and lost the other: an upright walking version with no fish left in it, then a fish missing the join between head and shoulders, then that join back but with toed feet, then a fully standing frog. Naming the tetrapod parts it must not have made it worse each round. Round five (2026-08-01), coelacanth-anchored and clear of neck/wrist/propped/limb: failed a third way — a small round-bodied orange reef fish, side-set eyes, no flattening to the head at all, nothing coelacanth-shaped beyond a vaguely lobed fin. Naming the coelacanth was not enough; the head's actual shape needs a second, independent anchor next round — e.g. a hammerhead shark's flattened head-plane, or a duck-billed platypus's flat broad snout, held next to the coelacanth's body and tail so the departure is anchored on both ends instead of asserted once. Round six (2026-08-01) took that anchor and the steel-blue colour landed, but the head came back barely flattened with the eyes still set on the sides — six rounds have now asked for a flattened head in a SIDE view and six have drawn an ordinary fish head. Round seven changes the viewpoint instead of the adjectives: seen from directly overhead, the flat plate is the only surface facing the viewer and both eyes have nowhere to sit but on top of it, so the diagnostic is forced by the framing rather than requested. The head is a smooth rounded spade, never a hammerhead's T-bar with side lobes and never eyes on stalks. The whole animal stays a coelacanth's deep steel-blue mottled with pale blue-white, never the orange of round five's reef fish.
arrivals.reference: Tiktaalik roseae holotype photographs and reconstructions — Daeschler et al. 2006, *Nature*; Field Museum; coelacanth (*Latimeria*) reference photographs, NOAA Fisheries / Smithsonian Ocean

arrivals.name: The coal forests
arrivals.line: Trees 40 metres tall, in swamps that become every coal seam on Earth. The air is 30% oxygen and the dragonflies are 70 cm across.
arrivals.analogy: a giant dragonfly, long segmented body, two pairs of long net-veined wings held flat to the sides
arrivals.negative: not modern dragonfly proportions — enormous, wingspan wider than a hawk's, same basic wing shape

arrivals.name: *Dimetrodon*
arrivals.line: Not a dinosaur. A synapsid — our own branch, 60 million years before the first dinosaur.
arrivals.analogy: a lizard-like animal with a tall sail of skin down its back, held up by long spines
arrivals.negative: not a dinosaur — it walks with a sprawling reptile-like gait, and it predates dinosaurs entirely

arrivals.name: The Great Dying
arrivals.line: Siberian basalt cooks the ocean. 81% of marine species die, in about 60,000 years — one and a half pixels.
arrivals.analogy: a thick slab of flood-basalt crust broken open, its top a ropy wrinkled skin in a cool pewter-grey, buckled into coils and folds like thick rope laid side by side or the skin on cooled porridge, with a narrow orange glow showing only in the deep cracks between the crusted plates
arrivals.negative: not a volcano with a cone, not an eruption scene and not a landscape — the Siberian Traps were floods of lava across flat ground, not a mountain. One slab. The crust stays a cool mid-toned pewter grey with no brown in it, never near-black, and the glow is confined to narrow cracks.
arrivals.reference: pāhoehoe basalt crust photographs; Siberian Traps flood basalt specimens; Burgess et al. 2014, *PNAS*

arrivals.name: The first dinosaurs, and the first mammals
arrivals.line: Both lines appear inside the same eight million years. At this scale, the same moment.
arrivals.analogy: two small animals side by side at the same scale, overlapping slightly so they read as one group: a slender bipedal dinosaur in muted sage-olive green with a cream underside, on long hind legs with its tail held level behind it, and beside it a shrew-sized furry mammal in warm sandy cream, on four legs with a long pointed snout
arrivals.negative: not a large dinosaur and not a modern mouse — both are small and early. The dinosaur is lightly built and bipedal, never a bulky quadruped, and its tail is held level and never drags. The mammal is furry with a long pointed snout and small low ears, not a round-eared rodent. Neither is brown or rust — the pair's dominant colour is the dinosaur's sage-olive green — and neither may be near-black.
arrivals.reference: *Eoraptor* and *Herrerasaurus* reconstructions (Ischigualasto); *Morganucodon* reconstructions

arrivals.name: The Triassic–Jurassic extinction
arrivals.line: The Atlantic starts to open. Half of everything dies, and the dinosaurs inherit it.
arrivals.analogy: a phytosaur — a long low four-legged reptile whose snout is drawn out into a slender straight rod lined with small teeth, ending in a smooth solid rounded tip like the blunt end of a wooden spoon handle; set on top of the skull, directly between and just in front of the eyes, is a raised dome like a small volcano, and the two nostril openings sit on the summit of that dome, far back from the snout; four short legs, a long heavy tail, and a warm sandy bronze hide with soft darker bronze banding along the back; the eye is a small amber bead
arrivals.negative: not a modern crocodile, alligator or gharial, and the word gharial is deliberately not used in the description above because three rounds that did use it (2026-07-31, 2026-08-01) all drew one: a gharial carries its nostril at the very tip of its snout, which is the single feature that would make this animal the wrong animal. There is nothing whatsoever on the snout tip — no hole, no dot, no opening, no dark mark — and the only openings on the head sit on top of the raised dome back between the eyes. The eye is never a solid black dot, or the luminance key punches it out of the artwork. The snout is long and slender, not short and broad. The whole animal from snout tip to tail tip sits well inside its own quarter of the picture with clear empty space all around it. An earlier round drew a tailless animal that ran off its frame and baked cropped. The round that shipped failed a further way: nothing near-black was ever asked for, and 2.4% of its own area keyed out into interior holes that the halo then filled with light, while the 3:1 boundary gate scored it a comfortable 4.17:1. Keep the whole animal light-to-mid in value, and render the shadow under the jaw, between the legs and along the tail as a shade or two darker than the bronze, never as a dark hollow.
arrivals.reference: Phytosaur skull and skeletal reconstructions — *Smilosuchus*, *Rutiodon*; Stocker & Butler 2013, *Geol. Soc. Lond. Spec. Publ.* 379

arrivals.name: *Archaeopteryx*
arrivals.line: Feathers, and the first wing that works.
arrivals.analogy: a raven-sized dinosaur-like animal with sharp teeth in its jaws, a long bony tail trailing straight out behind with feathers running down either side of it, and broad rounded feathered wings — its plumage a deep iridescent blue-green shot with violet, like the sheen on a magpie's wing, with pale cream bars across the flight feathers
arrivals.negative: not a modern bird — teeth and a long bony tail, not a beak and a fan of tail feathers. Nothing near-black anywhere on it: the fossil melanosome evidence points to dark plumage, but the luminance key punches any region below about 14% lightness straight out of the artwork and the halo then fills the hole with light, so the iridescence is carried light-to-mid in value and the deepest darks go no further than a mid blue-green. The 2026-07-31 round shipped with 2.1% of its own area punched into interior holes for exactly this reason, and the 3:1 boundary gate scored it a comfortable 4.45:1 while it happened.
arrivals.reference: *Archaeopteryx lithographica* Berlin specimen HMN MB.Av.101 and the Thermopolis specimen; Carney et al. 2012, *Nat. Commun.* — melanosome evidence for dark plumage

arrivals.name: The first flowers
arrivals.line: *Archaefructus*: no petals yet, but a flower — the oldest anyone can date. Before this, nothing was in bloom.
arrivals.analogy: a slender aquatic stem in bright fresh yellow-green with finely divided feathery leaves, carrying along its upper length a row of small paired seed pods and bare stamens attached directly to the stem, with no petals anywhere
arrivals.negative: not a modern flower: no petals, no sepals, no bloom and no blossom shape of any kind. *Archaefructus* is a thin water plant whose reproductive parts sit bare along the stem. Not a lily, not a magnolia, not a daisy. Nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: Sun et al. 2002, *Science* — *Archaefructus sinensis* holotype

arrivals.name: *Tyrannosaurus rex*
arrivals.line: The last and largest of the tyrannosaurs, gone within two million years of the asteroid.
arrivals.source: Fowler 2017, *PLOS ONE* — Hell Creek Fm. and equivalents, 68–66 Ma
arrivals.analogy: a huge two-legged predator held horizontal like a see-saw balanced over its hips — spine level, a long tail carried straight out behind as a counterweight — thick and deep where it leaves the hips, tapering only gradually, never a thin whip — and a short deep S-curved neck carrying a massive blunt boxy head as long as the animal's own thigh, as deep from skull-top to jaw as a bathtub is deep, broad across the snout, its jaws slightly parted on thick conical teeth; the forelimbs are tiny and held to the chest, each ending in a simple two-pronged pincer like a pair of tongs, and the hind legs are thick and bird-like with three forward-facing toes; the animal is a muted slate-grey with dark rust-red banding down its back and flanks and a pale cream underside
arrivals.negative: not upright like a kangaroo, and the tail never drags on the ground — that reconstruction is a century out of date. Exactly two fingers on each hand, not three. No fur and no coat of feathers. Not green, not a lizard and not roaring. Not a tan or sandy-brown desert dinosaur, which is the default and which would collide with the dust-veiled Chicxulub disc arriving forty-nine pixels later: the dominant colour is a muted slate-grey. Keep it light-to-mid in value throughout. Round one (2026-08-01) got the horizontal posture, the level tail and the colour right, and failed on the two facts that make it a tyrannosaurid rather than a generic mid-sized theropod: three clawed fingers on each hand instead of two, and a small shallow head on a long shallow neck. Naming 'exactly two fingers, not three' did not work in either the low proof or the final — the same way naming Tiktaalik's missing tetrapod parts did not work. Round two states the hand as a positive shape instead (a two-pronged pincer, like tongs) and pins the skull's size to the thigh rather than calling it 'enormous'.
arrivals.reference: *Tyrannosaurus rex* skeletal mounts AMNH 5027 and FMNH PR2081; modern horizontal-posture reconstructions

arrivals.name: Chicxulub
arrivals.line: Everything larger than a badger dies.
arrivals.analogy: the whole Earth as a disc, most of it under heavy swirling white and grey-brown storm cloud and dust, one brilliant white-hot flash and an expanding pale ring spreading from a single point, with only broken fragments of green land and blue ocean showing through the gaps
arrivals.negative: not a clean blue-and-green globe with recognisable continents — cloud and dust cover most of the disc and the coastlines are broken up and mostly hidden, so no continent is identifiable and no modern shape can be read off it. No night side, no crescent, no dark limb, and nothing anywhere on the disc may be black or near-black. Three rounds (2026-07-31) drew the modern world whenever the palaeogeography was prompted explicitly, however forcefully it was forbidden, so the geography is now veiled by the event itself rather than drawn — which is what the other three planet portraits already do (§11).

arrivals.name: The first true primates
arrivals.line: *Teilhardina* — not the primate-like mammals that came before it, but the first crown primate. It appears on three continents within 25,000 years, during a sudden burst of global heat.
arrivals.source: Smith, Rose & Gingerich 2006, *PNAS* — Teilhardina, PETM onset ~56 Ma
arrivals.analogy: a small squirrel-sized animal gripping a branch, its hands and feet wrapped right around it, with a narrow pointed furry muzzle like a squirrel's, a small rounded head, large forward-facing eyes, short soft fur in a warm chestnut-red with a cream belly, and a long slender tail held out for balance
arrivals.negative: not a monkey, not a marmoset, not a tamarin and not a ring-tailed lemur, which is the default and which a low proof of this subject drew (2026-08-01): it has no flat monkey face, no bare or brightly-coloured facial skin, no pale rings around the eyes and no large round side-set ears. An early primate is small, generalised and squirrel-like, and its face comes to a soft furry point. Not a rodent either — the giveaway is grasping hands with real fingers curled round the branch, and eyes facing forward rather than out to the sides. The chestnut is warm and muted, not a hot saturated orange. Nothing near-black.
arrivals.reference: *Teilhardina* and *Carpolestes* reconstructions; Bloch & Boyer 2002, *Science*

arrivals.name: Antarctica freezes
arrivals.line: The greenhouse world ends. The modern icehouse begins.
arrivals.analogy: a slab of ice calving off a dark rock cliff into the sea
arrivals.negative: not a whole ice-covered planet like Snowball Earth — one coastal cliff, one iceberg

arrivals.name: The human line splits from the chimpanzees
arrivals.line: Everything you would call human happens after this point — the next 175 pixels.
arrivals.analogy: a single ape skull in three-quarter view, warm ivory bone-cream throughout: a low rounded braincase, a heavy continuous brow ridge above the eyes, a short flat face and a broad palate of small worn teeth
arrivals.negative: not a modern human skull with a high domed forehead, and not a modern chimpanzee — this is the common ancestor's grade, so the braincase stays low and the brow heavy. No flesh, no hair and no ape-man portrait. The eye sockets, the nose opening and the gaps between the teeth are filled with a soft pale shadow only a shade or two darker than the surrounding bone — never dark hollows, never brown or black openings, and never a glimpse of empty space behind them. A low proof (2026-08-01) drew the orbits as near-black holes, which the luminance key punches straight out of the artwork and the halo then fills with light, so this is the one thing on this subject that must not be got wrong.
arrivals.reference: *Sahelanthropus tchadensis* cranium TM 266-01-060-1; Brunet et al. 2002, *Nature*

withheldNote: Held back from the scroll entirely, delivered in the finale fan. Label + date only. No line, no art, ever. Fan rows keep the point date (§8) — which is why `Fire, kept` shows `~800 ka` rather than the card notation `≥ 800 ka` it would carry if it had a card.

withheld.name: *Ardipithecus* walks upright
withheld.analogy: a small ape standing upright on two legs, seen from the side, both feet planted flat on the ground, long arms hanging free past its knees, a low forehead and a projecting muzzle, and a big toe that sticks out sideways from the foot like a thumb
withheld.negative: It stands tall on its two hind legs with its hands empty in the air, well clear of the ground. It is a flat simplified painting built from a few masses of colour, with no skin texture, no wrinkles and no photographic detail.

withheld.name: The first stone tools
withheld.analogy: a fist-sized grey river cobble with a few broad flakes knocked off one edge, leaving a rough zig-zag working edge, and one sharp pale flake lying beside it
withheld.negative: It is not a smooth teardrop-shaped hand-axe and it is not a polished stone axe head on a handle.

withheld.name: The first *Homo*
withheld.analogy: the head of an early human in profile facing right, with a sloping forehead, a heavy ridge of bone jutting over the eye, almost no chin, and short mid-brown hair
withheld.negative: It is a flat simplified painting built from a few masses of colour, with no skin texture, no wrinkles and no photographic detail. It is a side profile, not a front-facing portrait, and not a grey museum skull.

withheld.name: *Homo erectus*
withheld.analogy: the head of an early human in profile facing right, with a long low skull running far back, a straight heavy brow like a shelf over the eye, a broad flat nose and short mid-brown hair
withheld.negative: It is a flat simplified painting built from a few masses of colour, with no skin texture, no wrinkles and no photographic detail. It is a side profile of the head and shoulders only, not a full-length body and not a front-facing portrait.

withheld.name: Fire, kept
withheld.analogy: a shallow ring of pale rounded stones holding a small bright fire, orange and yellow flame standing up from a bed of warm grey ash
withheld.negative: It is not a big camp bonfire with logs stacked in a tepee, and there is no cave wall or campsite behind it.

withheld.name: *Homo sapiens*
withheld.analogy: the head of a modern human in profile facing right, with a high domed forehead rising straight above the eye, a small chin that juts forward and short mid-brown hair
withheld.negative: It is a flat simplified painting built from a few masses of colour, with no skin texture, no wrinkles and no photographic detail. It is a side profile, not a front-facing likeness of a particular person.

withheld.name: The oldest known picture
withheld.analogy: a fat wild pig with a bristly back and a short snout, painted in flat earth-red pigment that is patchy and faded, thin in places and worn away in others, as if brushed onto stone by hand a very long time ago
withheld.negative: It is a worn hand-made painting of a pig, not a smooth even illustration of a living animal. It is not drawn in outline, and it is not a wall covered in a scene of many animals — it is one painted pig alone.

withheld.name: Farming
withheld.analogy: a bundle of ripe golden wheat ears with their long whiskers fanning out, tied at the middle, and a curved pale wooden sickle laid across it
withheld.negative: It is not a field of crops, a farmhouse, or a tractor.

withheld.name: Writing
withheld.analogy: a small pale clay tablet the size of a palm, its face divided by faint ruled lines into a few rows of wedge marks, each wedge a small triangle with a thin tail and each one turned a different way
withheld.negative: The wedges vary in size and direction and sit in ruled rows, not in an even repeating grid. There are no letters of any alphabet, no readable characters and no hieroglyphs. It is not a scroll, a book or a carved stone monument.

withheld.name: The industrial revolution
withheld.analogy: a squat red-brick chimney stack with a pale grey plume of smoke curling off the top, a riveted warm-grey iron boiler at its foot and a big spoked flywheel beside it
withheld.negative: It is not a whole factory building or a city skyline, and it is not a steam locomotive.

fieldNote: The field keyframes (spec §6). Colour is a DATA CHANNEL: the background is the era's actual
sky and ocean colour, so it is a scientific claim and cannot drift into a decorative rainbow.
Every transition takes its TRUE duration in pixels — no arbitrary easing, no announced cuts —
so the drift RATE is itself a data channel. Pixel positions are derived from `ma`, never stored.
`origin` records where each value came from: `prototype` = the cadence prototype's measured table;
`spec` = forced by a §6 rider; `approved` = authored here from §6's words and signed off by Dustin 2026-07-31.

field.note: dim grey-white, thick steam and cloud / first ocean, dark
the hazy state, held — the flicker cannot be drawn / green
the last hazy state — the GOE clearing starts here / green
haze gone for good, clear blue / still green
blue / still green — banded iron is still running
blue / ocean has finished turning green → blue
held, pre-freeze — Snowball is a flash, not a stretch
Sturtian — sky deep BLUE (§6 rider), the white belongs to the ice
the ice breaks for good / Ediacaran sea
one slow ramp to daylight — solar luminosity really does rise ~30% MODELLED

finaleNote: The finale (spec §9). Beat lengths are in px from RUN_END and sum to FINALE.
`drainPad` is added to the 7 Ma card's overrun: the card lands at 116,425 and wants 660px of
dwell, so it releases 485px into the finale and the drain runs 485 + 40 = 525px (§9 staging 1).
Two beats are deliberately empty. §15: cutting either one will be proposed and must be refused.
The copy is verbatim from §8 and every number in it is recomputed from `constants` by the
tests — two of them were wrong in an earlier prototype.
copy.epilogue CUT 2026-07-31: its claim (T. rex and the first primates could not fit) went
false once both became real arrivals (Dustin's call). RESOLVED 2026-08-01, Dustin's call:
flip the story instead of dropping it — both stayed by breaking the 600px floor (§7) on
purpose, at 49px and 251px from Chicxulub. Numbers recomputed from `constants` by the tests,
same as the rest of this copy.

_comment: The plate's five paragraphs, lifted out of index.astro's markup 2026-08-06 so the
MODEL and the MARKUP cannot describe different text. `blipBandHeight` has read the
finale's copy from `finale.copy` since it was written, for exactly this reason; the
Boring Billion plate was solved against a share of the stage instead and never read
its own words at all. `body` is an array because its line breaks are AUTHORED —

index.astro joins it with
, and each entry wraps on its own.
boringBillion.title: The Boring Billion
body: Nothing much happens for a thousand million years.

copy.seamCaption: never drawn on the page you just scrolled.
copy.closing: The last ten happened in the final 110 of 115,000 pixels. Everything humans have farmed, written, built or remembered is the last three tenths of one pixel.
copy.epilogue: Two things on this page came within a rule of being cut. *Tyrannosaurus rex* sits 49 pixels from the asteroid; the first primates sit 251 — both closer than the 600-pixel floor allows anywhere else on this page, and both stayed anyway.
